leads.title: Qualify a per-platform notebook execution isolation backend
evidence: S05 establishes that Jupyter Server access permits arbitrary code execution; it does not validate a proposed sandbox.
leads.question: Which maintained OS sandbox/VM can enforce no network, read-only source mounts, private writable staging, CPU/memory/process/disk limits, descendant cancellation, and safe Jupyter Server/kernel operation on each team OS?
leads.next_step: Build a threat model and test profile for each supported OS. Until a profile passes, keep project viewing/editing available and disable execution on that OS.

leads.title: Resolve exact compatible runtime and environment-lock format
evidence: S01-S05 and S11 document relevant component APIs/version labels, but no captured evidence proves one installed compatibility tuple.
leads.question: What exact CPython patch, JupyterLab/Server, ipykernel, jupyter-client, nbformat, nbclient, DuckDB wheel/engine, native libraries, platform, and lock metadata form the supported build?
leads.next_step: Create one locked build and run the compatibility qualification in V01; pin package artifacts and record platform/native-library identity.

leads.title: Measure the 5 GB envelope by query shape
evidence: S09 documents spill support and explicit exceptions; S10 documents additional memory-limit caveats.
leads.question: Which bounded, streaming, and spill-supported CSV/NDJSON/Parquet plans meet latency, RSS, temporary-disk, and responsiveness limits on the target workstation?
leads.next_step: Run the synthetic and representative 5 GB plan matrix from V04; include combined blockers, pivot/list aggregates, Python materialization, and disk exhaustion.

leads.title: Preserve source-level missing/null and schema-evolution semantics
evidence: S07 documents that typed JSON reading maps missing keys to SQL NULL and that multi-file inference/union are bounded or opt-in.
leads.question: Which parser path preserves field-presence and raw values when analysts need missing distinct from explicit null, especially across multiple changing files?
leads.next_step: Prototype raw-object/presence-column capture in the chosen DuckDB build and test schema changes beyond sample limits; otherwise label the typed projection as intentionally collapsing absent/null.

leads.title: Validate row identity and order metadata through transformations
evidence: S08 describes operator-specific order preservation and limitations for joins, grouping, and tied sorts.
leads.question: Can the selected readers and transform wrappers preserve stable source locators through CSV quoted records, Parquet row groups, joins, and aggregation without materializing the input?
leads.next_step: Specify and test source-ordinal/key propagation and whether a total output ordering key exists; disable row-level diff where identity cannot be proved.

leads.title: Turn CSV sniffing into a reviewable import recipe
evidence: S06 documents sniff_csv output, suggested read command, sample scope, and user overrides.
leads.question: Can the UI make detected delimiter/header/types and the sniffing sample scope understandable, editable, and persist them as the accepted contract?
leads.next_step: Prototype the import dialog and ensure a sample-derived recipe remains provisional until full validation.

leads.title: Qualify Arrow interop for bounded result exchange
evidence: S11 documents querying Arrow/Pandas/Polars data and result conversion. No Arrow performance claim is made.
leads.question: Which Arrow reader/writer paths allow bounded batch handoff without materializing a 5 GB table in Python, and how are schema/null semantics preserved?
leads.next_step: Compare batch APIs and measure memory/copy behavior in the pinned environment before promising zero-copy or streaming behavior.

leads.title: Compare a thin CLI replay-first delivery
evidence: S02 establishes the .ipynb interchange structure; S03 documents sequential execution and hooks.
leads.question: Can a local CLI plus nbclient and the project manifest prove the import/replay/provenance core before a unified visual notebook pane is built?
leads.next_step: Prototype as a bounded alternative and compare implementation cost/accessibility against the integrated JupyterLab status/preview UX; retain the standard notebook format either way.
leads.state: alternative to evaluate; not selected for minimum workflow

leads.title: Compare a Python-dataframe-first engine alternative
leads.question: Would a Python-native lazy/batch engine better fit analyst-authored transforms, and what SQL interoperability and out-of-core trade-offs would result?
leads.next_step: If SQL usage or DuckDB compatibility testing becomes a blocker, independently inspect a primary-source Polars/Arrow implementation and benchmark the same workload matrix. This lead is not source-backed in the current proposal and is not a claim about capabilities.

leads.title: Review rich output portability and safe rendering
evidence: S02 documents multiple notebook output representations; the proposed renderer restrictions are product security choices, not established by that format description.
leads.question: Which MIME types (images, HTML/SVG, widgets) should be portable, safely rendered, and included in comparison digests?
leads.next_step: Define a minimal allowlist, sanitize or isolate active output, set size limits, and test across supported notebook viewers.

leads.title: Test filesystem locking and atomic commit across exchange media
leads.question: Which local filesystems and ordinary folder/bundle workflows provide the needed rename, fsync, and advisory-lock behavior?
leads.next_step: Fault-inject interrupted saves and concurrent writes on supported local filesystems. Treat network/shared filesystem synchronization as unsupported until separately qualified.

leads.title: Optional collaboration, hosted execution, scheduling, and more kernels
leads.question: Would any of these later features materially improve this small local team workflow after provenance and isolation are established?
leads.next_step: Do not build into the minimum plan; revisit only from team usage evidence and a separate threat/operations assessment.
